articles.title: Dark matter bound-states made easy
articles.summary: A light force carrier can mediate long-range interactions between dark matter particles and facilitate the formation of bound states. articles.title: Less Decoder is More Encoder: Geometric Representation Learning from Novel View Synthesis
articles.summary: This paper examines the role of Novel View Synthesis (NVS) in geometric representation learning. In principle, NVS should reason about 3D scene structure, thereby enabling transferable multi-view geometric representations. Yet, existing encoder-based NVS methods yield poor representations. articles.title: MoSE3: Learning World-Space SE(3) at Every Pixel
articles.summary: Dense 3D point tracking has been a prominent paradigm for modeling motion in dynamic scenes, but a point track is just a 3-DoF translation curve per pixel: it captures where pixels go, not the rotation of the underlying part, nor which pixels move together as one body. We propose MoSE3, the first feed-forward model that predicts dense SE(3) motion from monocular RGB video, producing full 6-DoF rigid transforms at every pixel in world space. articles.title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
articles.summary: We introduce 4DCodeBench, a benchmark for 4D inverse graphics through code generation, in which agents reconstruct dynamic scenes from video as executable graphics programs. To accomplish this, agents must translate visual observations into compact representations of scene structure and dynamics, by implementing abstractions such as physical simulations to reproduce complex behavior. articles.title: SpiderCSS: Scalable Fault-Tolerant CSS State Preparation
articles.summary: Fault-tolerant preparation of logical states is a critical primitive for the realization of large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing. This paper introduces SpiderCSS, a scalable compilation pipeline that generates highly-optimized, fault-tolerant state preparation circuits for arbitrary Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes. articles.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
articles.summary: Continual learning treats degradation on previously seen data as evidence of failure, a convention inherited from settings with a stationary prediction target, where a correct label remains correct indefinitely. World models do not satisfy this condition. articles.title: RNADyn: A Benchmark for Generating and Understanding RNA Dynamics
articles.summary: Ribonucleic acid (RNA) functions through conformational changes that are not fully captured by static structures. However, large-scale standardized RNA dynamics data remain limited, and existing approaches typically treat trajectory generation and dynamics understanding as separate objectives. Here, we introduce RNADynBench, a standardized RNA molecular dynamics (MD) benchmark with 2585 quality-controlled 100-ns all-atom trajectories and leakage-controlled splits. articles.title: From Mixing to Tearing: Graph Decomposition in Decentralized Optimization via Message Passing
articles.summary: We study the minimization of sums of smooth strongly convex functions over undirected graphs, with each function held by one agent and communication restricted to neighbors in the graph. articles.summary: In this paper we discuss the quasinormal modes and the tidal responses of a four-dimensional asymptotically flat Reissner-Nördstrom black hole near extremality and investigate the nontrivial near-horizon quantum corrections of these observables. articles.summary: We prove the first quantitative bounds for the Gowers norms of the von Mangoldt function minus a Siegel corrected model function in short intervals. articles.title: Unitary complexity in polynomial space
articles.summary: We show that if quantum commitments exist, then either there is no polynomial-time solution to the unitary synthesis problem, or $\mathsf{BPP} \neq \mathsf{NEXP}$. Thus, showing unconditionally that quantum commitments exist would require answering at least one of two longstanding open questions in complexity theory. articles.title: Fractal dimension of critical Gaussian free field sign clusters
articles.summary: We study metric graph sign clusters of the Gaussian free field on a large class of transient weighted graphs $G$ that are sufficiently low-dimensional, i.e. below the mean-field regime, and prove a macroscopic equivalence property: several natural ways to define macroscopic clusters - involving any of diameter, volume, or capacity functionals - are in fact the same. articles.title: LESSER: Post-Training Data Selection with Output-Layer Gradients
articles.summary: The choice of post-training data for large language models substantially affects downstream performance. Gradient-based data selection is a popular approach that ranks training data by how well their gradients align with those of a small validation set. articles.title: Decoding the Functional Roles of Register and High-Norm Patch Tokens in Vision Transformers
articles.summary: Self-supervised Vision Transformers (ViTs), such as DINOv2, learn rich visual representations, but the functions of their internal tokens remain poorly understood. Recent architectures introduce dedicated register tokens to reduce high-norm out- lier patch tokens that emerge in background re- gions, yet the semantic and functional roles of both token types have not been fully established. articles.title: On The Complexity of Redundancy-Free Quantum Hamiltonians

articles.title: Maximum-Entropy Extension of Quantum Correlation Functions from Short Real-Time Dynamics
articles.summary: Correlation functions are central to understanding the behavior of quantum systems, with their spectra giving direct access to quasiparticle and collective excitations. articles.title: Language Models that Play Chess and Explain Their Moves
articles.summary: Modern chess engines are silent experts: they play at a superhuman level, but do not offer explanations for their play. On the other hand, language models (LMs) can generate plausible-sounding explanations, but their weak playing strength limits the utility of their explanations. articles.title: Transcriptome-informed multi-modal AI for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response from breast cancer biopsies
articles.summary: Scarcity of labeled data limits development of deep learning biomarkers in oncology. We develop a two-stage AI model predicting pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer. articles.title: FlowHMR: Physically Plausible Motion Capture from Video
articles.summary: We present FlowHMR, a framework for recovering physically plausible global 3D human motion from monocular video. Previous learning-based methods typically regress human motion directly from video and train the network with geometric supervision. articles.title: SigLIP2 for aerial fire risk classification
articles.summary: We examine the transfer of a pretrained SigLIP2 image encoder to seven class fire risk classification from aerial imagery. We introduce a reproducible partition of the public FireRisk training mirror and an implementation that records data provenance, preprocessing and model selection. Two initial runs compare a frozen encoder probe with full model adaptation. On the validation partition, full adaptation reaches 63.05% accuracy and 58.94% macro F1, compared with 55.95% and 50.19% for the probe.

articles.title: Efficient Block Encoding of Structured Hamiltonians by Separating Where and What
articles.summary: Fault-tolerant block encodings of structured Hamiltonians can reduce their non-Clifford cost in SELECT by selecting where an operator acts separately from what is applied. We construct permute-act-unpermute circuits whose CSWAP networks exploit the support geometry: a selected support is brought to a fixed target register, a shared local circuit acts there, and the permutation is undone. articles.title: Does a mortality schedule need a Makeham term? Calibrating the likelihood-ratio test
articles.summary: Whether a fitted mortality model needs a Makeham term, the non-negative constant representing background mortality, is commonly decided with a likelihood-ratio test. articles.title: Simulation-Free Learning of Population Dynamics with Wasserstein Lagrangian Residuals
articles.summary: The dynamics of cells, organisms, and fluids are often modeled as probability distributions evolving over time. Reconstructing and extrapolating this evolution from unpaired snapshots requires assumptions about the underlying process. articles.title: Finite-momentum pairing and magnetic halos in a spin-imbalanced Holstein model
articles.summary: Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) superconductivity, Cooper pairing at finite-momentum driven by spin imbalance, remains difficult to study numerically in two dimensions. articles.title: FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution
articles.summary: LLM-guided evolutionary methods, such as AlphaEvolve, have emerged as powerful approaches for challenging computational optimization problems, such as circle packing. However, prior work typically optimizes performance gain over a fixed number of iterations. We argue that practical optimization should maximize gain per unit cost. articles.title: Quantum Simulation on Riemannian Manifolds
articles.summary: We investigate algorithms for the quantum simulation of the Schrödinger equation on a Riemannian manifold, where the kinetic operator is defined by the Laplace--Beltrami operator corresponding to the metric. articles.title: Ordering-Aware Theory of Trotter Error

articles.title: Optimal kernel functions for linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation
articles.summary: Linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation (LCHS) provides an asymptotically optimal framework for the quantum simulation of linear non-unitary dynamics. articles.title: Planning to Learn
articles.summary: Policy-gradient methods are central to modern reinforcement learning, including LLM post-training. When they struggle, the usual suspects are exploration, credit assignment and action-sampling noise. Classification has none of them. articles.summary: Masked diffusion language models (dLMs) offer a promising parallel alternative to autoregressive models for complex reasoning. articles.summary: Autoregressive (AR) video models excel at causal generation, but their reliance on next-chunk prediction confines them to a short-sighted, reactive paradigm. articles.summary: Deploying a new decision policy creates a cold-start problem for prediction models whose targets depend on the policy's actions: historical observations reflect earlier policies, while real observations under the new policy are not yet available. articles.summary: We study single-sample prophet inequalities for online combinatorial allocation. articles.summary: Multi-pitch estimation in vocal ensembles is challenging because singers occupy overlapping pitch ranges and often sing at closely spaced fundamental frequencies, causing their harmonics to overlap in time-frequency representations. articles.title: MRVQ: One Resident Index for Dimension- and Rate-Elastic Vector Search
articles.summary: Dense-retrieval services must switch among embedding-prefix dimensions and index bit rates as latency, quality, and memory budgets change. articles.title: PoCoFL: POlicy-COmpliant Federated Learning
articles.summary: Federated Learning (FL) is a privacy-oriented learning paradigm that enables collaborative model training while keeping training data local to participating clients. articles.title: On-Board Anomaly Detection for Efficient Marine Environmental Monitoring
articles.summary: Marine ecosystems are impacted by various threats such as oil spills, algal blooms, and sediment floods, which disrupt habitats, wildlife, and human activities.
